Fact.Name: The employers a filer under-reported tips to, one row per employer (Form 4137 line 1)
Fact.Description:
The per-employer collection the printed line-1 table holds: "Complete a separate row for each employer" (lines 79-80). Each row carries the four printed columns — (a) the employer's name, (b) their identification number, (c) total cash and charge tips received from them, (d) total cash and charge tips reported to them — plus the spouse whose Form 4137 the row belongs on.
NO INTAKE ASKS IT TODAY, so an unanswered collection is the normal state and most committed scenarios leave it so; the collection root then resolves Incomplete and is omitted from every snapshot. That state is safe because it is the THIRD arm of lines 2 and 3, the complete-safe $0 — the footing arm fires only when this root IS answered, and each row's amount is read through a complete-safe ../totalTipsReceivedOrZero or ../tipsReportedToEmployerOrZero so a partly filled row cannot make a line Incomplete. Modelling the intake before a screen exists is the BUILD-FIRST directive's instruction, and it is what lets the employer names and identification numbers be carried at all.

Fact.Name: Column (a): the employer's name
Fact.Description:
Column (a) of the printed line-1 row: "Name of employer to whom you were required to but didn't report all your tips". The instruction ties it to the W-2: "Enter your employer's name exactly as shown on your Form W-2" (lines 88-89).
NOT LINKED TO /formW2s, and that is a decision rather than an omission. The employer a filer under-reported tips to need not have issued a Form W-2 this return carries — the printed instruction says to copy the name off the W-2 when there is one, not that there always is one — so a CollectionItem link into /formW2s would refuse rows the form admits. The name is carried as text, exactly as formW2s:/formW2s/*/employerName carries it.
THE MaxLength BOUND IS COPIED FROM THAT FACT; ITS Match REGEX IS NOT, and the omission is deliberate. formW2s:/formW2s/*/employerName restricts its character set because it is the source of an MeF employer-name ELEMENT, which is why formW2s:/formW2s/*/mefEmployerNameLine1 exists to strip what the regex still admits. This column is not that element — it is a line on a Form 4137 the printed instruction routes to an attachment — so importing a transmission-format constraint would refuse names the paper form accepts. If a future MeF surface needs the narrower set, the place for it is a derived strip fact of the mefEmployerNameLine1 shape, not a limit on the intake.

Fact.Name: Column (b): the employer's identification number, or the words "Applied For"
Fact.Description: Column (b) of the printed line-1 row. NOT AN EIN TYPE, and the printed instruction is why: "enter the employer identification number (EIN) or the words 'Applied For' exactly as shown on your Form W-2" (lines 90-92). A typed EIN writable could not hold the second alternative, and the alternative is not an edge case — it is what a filer copies off a W-2 issued before the employer's EIN came through. Carried as text for that reason, bounded at 11 characters, which is the longer of a formatted EIN (XX-XXXXXXX, 10) and the literal words (11).

Fact.Name: Column (c): total cash and charge tips received from this employer
Fact.Description:
Column (c) of the printed line-1 row: "Total cash and charge tips you received (including unreported tips)". The instruction for columns (c) and (d) lists four kinds of tip that must be included, among them the ones never reported at all and the ones under the $20 monthly threshold (lines 93-119), so this figure is the GROSS receipt from this employer and not a residual.
SIGN: NON-NEGATIVE, carried as a declared Limit. No upper bound is declared: the printed column has none. The rows DO sum to line 2 through ../totalTipsReceivedOrZero whenever the filer leaves the line-2 attestation blank; where the attestation is made it wins, and the table may then legitimately be a partial decomposition of it.
NOT FOR RRTA TIPS. "Don't use Form 4137 to report tips received for work covered by the Railroad Retirement Tax Act. To get railroad retirement credit, you must report these tips to your employer." (lines 106-109.) Nothing in this dictionary tags a tip as RRTA-covered and no document reports it, so the rule can only be carried as the instruction the filer reads before entering the amount.
INCLUDES W-2 BOX 8 ALLOCATED TIPS. Column (c) counts "Tips you didn't report at all (include any allocated tips (see Allocated tips, earlier) shown on your Form(s) W-2, box 8, unless you can prove that your unreported tips are less than the amount in box 8). Include these tips in column (c)." (lines 111-114.) This row's figure must already contain this employer's box 8 amount, added to any other tips never reported. A filer whose rows leave box 8 out answers No to /writablePrimaryFilerTotalTipsIncludesAllocatedTips (or its secondary twin), and line 2 then adds the filer's box 8 total.
NOT FOR A MISCLASSIFIED WORKER. A worker paid on Form 1099-MISC or Form 1099-NEC who believes they are an employee does not use this form "to report the social security and Medicare tax on that income. Instead, use Form 8919" (lines 64-66).

Fact.Name: Column (d): total cash and charge tips reported to this employer
Fact.Description:
Column (d) of the printed line-1 row: "Total cash and charge tips you reported to your employer". On a correctly prepared row this is a subset of column (c), which is why the return-level line 4 (line 2 less line 3) has no printed floor — but NO ROW-LEVEL RELATION IS ENFORCED HERE, deliberately. A row-level refusal would reject a filer whose table is a partial decomposition of an attested combined total, which the printed more-than-five-employers instruction expressly permits, and the return-level floor on line 4 already catches the transposition this would guard against.
SIGN: NON-NEGATIVE, carried as a declared Limit.

Fact.Name: Column (c) for this row, complete-safe: the tips received, or $0 when the cell is blank
Fact.Description:
The ADDEND form of column (c): ../writableTotalTipsReceived when the cell is answered and $0 when it is not, so that the line-2 CollectionSums over /primaryFilerForm4137Employers and /secondaryFilerForm4137Employers stay Complete on a table whose rows are only partly filled in. Built to form8919:/form8919Firms/*/wagesOrZero's shape, which is this dictionary's precedent for a complete-safe per-item addend on a printed row table.
CENTS ARE PRESERVED ON PURPOSE. This fact carries no Round; the single Round sits on /primaryFilerForm4137Line2 and /secondaryFilerForm4137Line2, which is what i1040gi page 23 requires of a line built by addition: "If you have to add two or more amounts to figure the amount to enter on a line, include cents when adding the amounts and round off only the total." Do NOT use this fact for the printed column (c) cell — the register prints ../writableTotalTipsReceived.

Fact.Name: Column (d) for this row, complete-safe: the tips reported, or $0 when the cell is blank
Fact.Description:
The ADDEND form of column (d), the twin of ../totalTipsReceivedOrZero: ../writableTipsReportedToEmployer when the cell is answered and $0 when it is not, so that the line-3 CollectionSums stay Complete on a partly filled table. A blank column (d) on a row whose column (c) is filled is the ordinary case this exists for — it is the filer who reported NOTHING to that employer, which is the population Form 4137 collects.
CENTS ARE PRESERVED, and the single Round sits on /primaryFilerForm4137Line3 and /secondaryFilerForm4137Line3; see ../totalTipsReceivedOrZero. Do NOT use this fact for the printed column (d) cell — the register prints ../writableTipsReportedToEmployer.

Fact.Name: Which spouse's Form 4137 this employer row belongs on
Fact.Description:
The per-row filer attribution, built to the shape scheduleH:/householdEmployees/*/writableEmployerFiler uses. Form 4137 is filed per spouse ("If married, complete a separate Form 4137 for each spouse with unreported tips", line 11), so an employer row belongs to one spouse's form, not to the return.
UNANSWERED IS THE PRIMARY FILER, which is exact for the single-filer and single-form majority: one Form 4137 means one set of rows and the attribution question never needs to be asked. The mirror is ../belongsToSecondaryFiler, which requires an ANSWERED value, so every row belongs to exactly one filer.

Fact.Name: This employer row is on the primary filer's Form 4137
Fact.Description: The primary half of the row attribution, built to the shape scheduleH:/householdEmployees/*/belongsToPrimaryFiler uses. AN UNANSWERED ../writableEmployerFiler counts as the primary filer, for the reason given there.

Fact.Name: This employer row is on the secondary filer's Form 4137
Fact.Description:
The secondary half of the row attribution. It requires an ANSWERED ../writableEmployerFiler, the mirror of ../belongsToPrimaryFiler's default, so that every row belongs to exactly one filer.
GUARDED ON /secondaryFiler'S OWN COMPLETENESS, which is what makes that "exactly one" claim true rather than merely intended. filers:/secondaryFiler resolves INCOMPLETE on a return whose /filers holds a single item, and a bare Equal against it is then Incomplete too — so an ANSWERED ../writableEmployerFiler on a single-filer return would carry that Incomplete into /secondaryFilerForm4137Employers and out through the secondary filer's lines 2 and 3. The guard is the FIRST conjunct so the All short-circuits on it. It is the shape form8919:/form8919Firms/*/belongsToSecondaryFiler already ships, for the same reason.
THE GUARD TESTS /filers CARDINALITY, NOT FILING STATUS: filers:/secondaryFiler resolves Complete on any return whose /filers holds two items, married or not, so this fact and the views it feeds resolve the same way for a second single-status filer as for an MFJ spouse. "Secondary filer" names the /filers collection's second item, not a marital relationship.
NO SUCH GUARD IS NEEDED ON THE PRIMARY SIDE: filers:/primaryFiler is Complete on every return, which is already what keeps ../belongsToPrimaryFiler Complete. Where no secondary filer exists, no row belongs to one. Pinned by tests/nodes/ty2025/form4137/f4137-single-filer-attributed-row-resolves.

Fact.Name: Primary filer's total cash and charge tips received in 2025 (Form 4137 line 2)
Fact.Description:
The primary filer's attested total of Form 4137 line 1 column (c) across every employer — all cash and charge tips received, INCLUDING the unreported ones. Optional: a filer with no unreported tips never answers it.
IT IS NO LONGER THE ONLY SOURCE OF LINE 2. This writable still WINS whenever it is answered, because the printed more-than-five-employers rule makes the attested figure the combined total of every Form 4137 and attached statement. Where it is UNANSWERED and /form4137Employers is answered, /primaryFilerForm4137Line2 adds this filer's own column (c) rows instead, because that is what the printed line says; with neither, it resolves $0. See /primaryFilerForm4137Line2.
NOT FOR RRTA TIPS. "Don't use Form 4137 to report tips received for work covered by the Railroad Retirement Tax Act. To get railroad retirement credit, you must report these tips to your employer." (lines 106-109.) Nothing in this dictionary tags a tip as RRTA-covered, so the rule is carried here, as the instruction the filer reads before entering the amount.
INCLUDES W-2 BOX 8 ALLOCATED TIPS. Column (c) counts "Tips you didn't report at all (include any allocated tips (see Allocated tips, earlier) shown on your Form(s) W-2, box 8, unless you can prove that your unreported tips are less than the amount in box 8). Include these tips in column (c)." (lines 111-114.) The filer's figure must already contain every employer's box 8 amount, added to any other tips never reported. A filer whose figure leaves box 8 out answers No to /writablePrimaryFilerTotalTipsIncludesAllocatedTips, and /primaryFilerForm4137Line2 then adds the box 8 total (/primaryFilerAllocatedTipsAddedToLineTwo); left unanswered on that population the return is refused (/knockoutForm4137AllocatedTipsInLineTwoUnanswered).
NOT FOR A MISCLASSIFIED WORKER. A worker paid on Form 1099-MISC or Form 1099-NEC who believes they are an employee does not use this form "to report the social security and Medicare tax on that income. Instead, use Form 8919" (lines 64-66).

Fact.Name: Secondary filer's total cash and charge tips received in 2025 (Form 4137 line 2)
Fact.Description: The secondary filer's twin of /writablePrimaryFilerTotalTipsReceived. Separate because the form is filed per spouse.

Fact.Name: Form 4137 line 2, primary filer
Fact.Description:
Form 4137 line 2: total cash and charge tips received in 2025, the line-1 column (c) total. Complete-safe — $0 when neither the attestation nor the table is answered.
THREE ARMS, and the order is the argument. THE FORM TEXT IS THE PROOF: line 2 reads "Total cash and charge tips you received in 2025. Add the amounts from line 1," / "column (c)" (lines 29-30). The FIRST arm is the attested /writablePrimaryFilerTotalTipsReceived, which still wins whenever it is answered, because the printed more-than-five-employers rule tells a filer with six or more employers to complete line 1 on additional forms and to put "the combined totals of all your Forms 4137 and attached statements" on the one form's lines 2 and 3 (lines 83-87): the attested total may legitimately exceed the five rows this collection prints, so it is the better statement of the line WHEN THE FILER MAKES IT. That rule defends the attestation winning when answered; it says nothing about the return that never answers it, where the table is the only statement of the amount. So the SECOND arm fires exactly when the writable is NOT complete and /form4137Employers IS, and adds this filer's own column (c) rows: CollectionSum over /primaryFilerForm4137Employers/*/totalTipsReceivedOrZero. The predicate is a real "was the source answered" test on a WRITABLE, never an IsComplete on a complete-safe derived fact, which would always be true. The THIRD arm is the unchanged complete-safe $0.
PER FILER, NOT PER RETURN, which is why the sum is over the FILTERED view: Form 4137 is filed per spouse (line 11), so the primary filer's line 2 may never pick up a row attributed to the secondary filer.
THE SINGLE Round IS DELIBERATE. /form4137Employers/*/totalTipsReceivedOrZero preserves cents so the Round applies to the total and not to each addend, which is what i1040gi page 23 requires of a line built by addition.

Fact.Name: Form 4137 line 2, secondary filer
Fact.Description:
Secondary-filer twin of /primaryFilerForm4137Line2. Same three arms in the same order: the attested /writableSecondaryFilerTotalTipsReceived when it is answered, else the sum of this filer's own column (c) rows (CollectionSum over /secondaryFilerForm4137Employers/*/totalTipsReceivedOrZero) when /form4137Employers is answered, else the complete-safe $0. See the primary twin for the printed line-2 text that proves the addition and for the more-than-five-employers rule that keeps the attested arm first.
ITS FILTERED VIEW IS EMPTY, NOT INCOMPLETE, ON A SINGLE-FILER RETURN, which is what keeps this fact Complete at $0 there: /form4137Employers/*/belongsToSecondaryFiler guards filers:/secondaryFiler's own completeness and resolves Complete false when no secondary filer exists, so /secondaryFilerForm4137Employers filters to nothing and the CollectionSum is $0.

Fact.Name: Primary filer's tips reported to employers in 2025 (Form 4137 line 3)
Fact.Description:
The primary filer's attested total of Form 4137 line 1 column (d) — the tips already reported to employers, which are therefore already inside Form W-2 box 1. Optional.
IT IS NO LONGER THE ONLY SOURCE OF LINE 3, on the same three arms as its line-2 twin: the attestation when answered, else this filer's own column (d) rows, else $0. See /primaryFilerForm4137Line3.
NOT FOR RRTA TIPS. Tips for work covered by the Railroad Retirement Tax Act are reported to the employer for railroad retirement credit and do not belong on this form at all (lines 106-109).

Fact.Name: Primary filer's reported-tip amount, floored at zero for Form 4137 line 3
Fact.Description: Complete-only nonnegative reader for /writablePrimaryFilerTipsReportedToEmployer. The writable declares a minimum of $0, and the reported-tip total is already included in wages, so a persisted negative answer must not increase unreported tips or reduce the related tax calculation. Unanswered input remains Incomplete.

Fact.Name: Secondary filer's tips reported to employers in 2025 (Form 4137 line 3)
Fact.Description: Secondary-filer twin of /writablePrimaryFilerTipsReportedToEmployer.

Fact.Name: Secondary filer's reported-tip amount, floored at zero for Form 4137 line 3
Fact.Description: Complete-only nonnegative reader for /writableSecondaryFilerTipsReportedToEmployer. The writable declares a minimum of $0, and the reported-tip total is already included in wages, so a persisted negative answer must not increase unreported tips or reduce the related tax calculation. Unanswered input remains Incomplete.

Fact.Name: Form 4137 line 3, primary filer
Fact.Description:
Form 4137 line 3: total cash and charge tips reported to the employer(s) in 2025, the line-1 column (d) total, on the same three arms as line 2 — the attested /writablePrimaryFilerTipsReportedToEmployer when it is answered, else CollectionSum over /primaryFilerForm4137Employers/*/tipsReportedToEmployerOrZero when /form4137Employers is answered, else the complete-safe $0. The printed line is "Add the amounts from line 1," / "column (d)" (lines 31-32) and the more-than-five-employers rule names lines 2 AND 3 together, so the two lines take the same shape for the same reason; see /primaryFilerForm4137Line2 for the full argument and the single-Round rule.
A BLANK COLUMN (d) ON A FILLED ROW IS $0, NOT A GAP — it is the filer who reported nothing to that employer, which is the population this form collects.

Fact.Name: Form 4137 line 3, secondary filer
Fact.Description: Secondary-filer twin of /primaryFilerForm4137Line3, over /secondaryFilerForm4137Employers/*/tipsReportedToEmployerOrZero. Complete at $0 on a single-filer return for the reason /secondaryFilerForm4137Line2 records.

Fact.Name: Primary filer has adequate records supporting unreported tips below W-2 box 8
Fact.Description: Optional attestation for the Form 4137 allocated-tips exception. If unanswered, box 8 remains the minimum. If true, the LINE 2 amount must also be supplied before the lower actual difference can control: a blank line 3 is $0 on the printed form and the exception still has its stated basis, but a blank line 2 would drop the box-8 floor to $0 on no stated basis at all.

Fact.Name: Secondary filer has adequate records supporting unreported tips below W-2 box 8
Fact.Description: The secondary-filer twin of /writablePrimaryFilerHasAdequateRecordsForAllocatedTips, including its line-2 condition.

Fact.Name: Primary filer can use the Form 4137 allocated-tips exception
Fact.Description: Complete-safe reading of the primary filer's adequate-records attestation. Unanswered is false, because the printed exception requires the filer to have records.

Fact.Name: Secondary filer can use the Form 4137 allocated-tips exception
Fact.Description: Secondary-filer twin of /primaryFilerHasAdequateRecordsForAllocatedTips.

Fact.Name: Primary filer's line 2 already includes the Form W-2 box 8 allocated tips
Fact.Description: QUESTION, asked when the primary filer's Forms W-2 show allocated tips in box 8, the adequate-records exception is not claimed, and line 2 is more than line 3: "Does your total of cash and charge tips received (Form 4137 line 2) already include the allocated tips shown in box 8 of your Forms W-2?" Column (c) includes box 8 allocated tips; No adds them to line 2. Unanswered on that population refuses the return through /knockoutForm4137AllocatedTipsInLineTwoUnanswered.

Fact.Name: Secondary filer's line 2 already includes the Form W-2 box 8 allocated tips
Fact.Description: The secondary-filer twin of /writablePrimaryFilerTotalTipsIncludesAllocatedTips, asked on the secondary filer's own Form 4137.

Fact.Name: Primary filer's box 8 allocated tips added to line 2
Fact.Description: The primary filer's Forms W-2 box 8 total when the filer answers that line 2 leaves those allocated tips out and does not claim the adequate-records exception, because column (c), and so line 2, includes them; $0 otherwise.

Fact.Name: Secondary filer's box 8 allocated tips added to line 2
Fact.Description: The secondary-filer twin of /primaryFilerAllocatedTipsAddedToLineTwo.

Fact.Name: Knockout: whether line 2 includes the box 8 allocated tips is unanswered
Fact.Description: Refuses a return on which a filer's Forms W-2 show allocated tips in box 8, the adequate-records exception is not claimed, line 2 is more than line 3, and the filer has not said whether line 2 already includes those allocated tips. Column (c) must include them; if line 2 does, line 4 is line 2 less line 3 and box 8 is only its floor, and if it does not, line 4 is that amount plus box 8. The two readings differ by up to the whole box 8 amount and nothing else on the return tells them apart, so the question is required. Answering it clears the refusal. Complete false whenever any of the conditions is known not to hold.

Fact.Name: Form 4137 line 4, primary filer (Form 1040 line 1c)
Fact.Description: Form 4137 line 4 = line 2 less line 3: the tips received but NOT reported to the employer. W-2 box 8 is the minimum when allocated tips exist, unless the filer attests that adequate records support a lower line-2-less-line-3 amount. This fact reads that complete-safe per-filer result from formW2s; it therefore carries both the Form 1040 line 1c income leg and the Form 4137 FICA chain. The underlying subtraction remains floored at zero so a transposed line 2/line 3 cannot create negative tip income.

Fact.Name: Form 4137 line 4, secondary filer (Form 1040 line 1c)
Fact.Description: Secondary-filer twin of /primaryFilerForm4137Line4, including the box-8 minimum and adequate-records exception.

Fact.Name: Primary filer's tips under the $20 monthly threshold (Form 4137 line 5)
Fact.Description: Tips the primary filer received but was NOT required to report because the month's total was under $20. These are excluded from social security and Medicare tax but remain income (they are already inside line 4). Optional.

Fact.Name: Primary filer's under-$20 tip amount, floored at zero for Form 4137 line 5
Fact.Description: Complete-only nonnegative reader for /writablePrimaryFilerTipsBelowTwentyDollarMonthlyThreshold. The writable declares a minimum of $0, and line 5 is subtracted from taxable unreported tips, so a persisted negative answer must not increase the Form 4137 tax. Unanswered input remains Incomplete.

Fact.Name: Secondary filer's tips under the $20 monthly threshold (Form 4137 line 5)
Fact.Description: Secondary-filer twin of /writablePrimaryFilerTipsBelowTwentyDollarMonthlyThreshold.

Fact.Name: Secondary filer's under-$20 tip amount, floored at zero for Form 4137 line 5
Fact.Description: Complete-only nonnegative reader for /writableSecondaryFilerTipsBelowTwentyDollarMonthlyThreshold. The writable declares a minimum of $0, and line 5 is subtracted from taxable unreported tips, so a persisted negative answer must not increase the Form 4137 tax. Unanswered input remains Incomplete.

Fact.Name: Form 4137 line 5, primary filer
Fact.Description: Form 4137 line 5: cash and charge tips received but not reported to the employer because the month's total was under $20. Complete-safe $0 unanswered, which is the correct default — a filer who does not claim the exclusion is taxed on the whole of line 4, the taxpayer-ADVERSE direction.

Fact.Name: Form 4137 line 5, secondary filer
Fact.Description: Secondary-filer twin of /primaryFilerForm4137Line5.

Fact.Name: Form 4137 line 6, primary filer (also Form 8959 line 2)
Fact.Description:
Form 4137 line 6 = line 4 less line 5: the unreported tips subject to MEDICARE tax. Medicare has no wage base, so this figure — not the social-security-capped line 10 — is what line 12 multiplies, and it is also the figure Form 8959 line 2 carries into the Additional Medicare Tax base ("Enter this amount on Form 8959, line 2, if you're required to file that form").
FLOORED AT ZERO on the same reasoning as line 4: line 5 is by construction a subset of line 4 (both are tips the filer did not report to the employer), the printed line carries no "if zero or less" clause, and an unfloored negative would flow into Form 8959's line-4 base and REDUCE Additional Medicare Tax — a false allowance. Floored, an over-stated line 5 costs the filer the social security and Medicare tax on tips they need not have excluded, which is taxpayer-adverse.

Fact.Name: Form 4137 line 6, secondary filer (also Form 8959 line 2)
Fact.Description: Secondary-filer twin of /primaryFilerForm4137Line6.

Fact.Name: Form 4137 line 6, both filers (Form 8959 line 2)
Fact.Description: Both filers' Form 4137 line 6, summed — the amount Form 8959 line 2 carries. Form 8959 is a RETURN-level form (one per return, with a joint threshold at line 5) while Form 4137 is filed per spouse, so the two per-filer line-6 figures add here. Complete-safe $0 on every return with no tip intake, which keeps Form 8959 line 4 and therefore Schedule 2 line 11 byte-identical on the committed corpus.

Fact.Name: Form 4137 line 7, maximum wages subject to social security tax
Fact.Description: Form 4137 line 7: the 2025 social security (OASDI) contribution and benefit base, $176,100, printed on the form itself. Not per filer — it is the same statutory figure on both spouses' forms; the per-person capping happens at line 9, which subtracts each filer's OWN line 8.

Fact.Name: Form 4137 line 8, primary filer
Fact.Description:
Form 4137 line 8: this filer's total social security wages and social security tips, "total of your Form(s) W-2, boxes 3 and 7". Summed over formW2s:/primaryFilerW2s — the filer's OWN W-2s — because the social security wage base is a per-person limit; a graph-wide sum over both spouses' W-2s would let one spouse's under-cap position mask the other's, exactly the error formW2s:/primaryFilerTotalOasdiWithholding's Description argues against for Schedule 3 line 11.
CENTS PRESERVED IN THE ADDENDS. It sums /formW2s/*/oasdiWagesUnrounded and /oasdiTipsUnrounded — the cents-bearing twins added with this fill — rather than the rounded per-W-2 entry facts, and rounds once here at the printed line. Line 8 is an "add two or more amounts" line in i1040gi page 23's sense, so summing already-rounded per-W-2 items is the construction that rule forbids; this is the same remedy already applied to boxes 5, 4 and 1. Both twins are complete-safe ($0 when the box is unanswered), so a CollectionSum over an empty or partly-answered set is Complete, and a return with no W-2 at all gives line 8 = $0 rather than Incomplete.
THE THIRD ADDEND IS THE RRTA TERM, and the printed line has always carried it: "...boxes 3 and 7) and railroad retirement (RRTA) compensation (subject to 6.2% rate)". It is this filer's box-14 railroad retirement compensation (formW2s:/formW2s/*/rrtaCompensationUnrounded), summed over that filer's own W-2s like the other two. It CANNOT double-count the box-3 term: the W-2 instructions reserve boxes 3 through 7 for social security and Medicare wages and say in terms that those boxes "are not to be used to report railroad retirement compensation and taxes", so a railroad employer's box 3 is empty and box 14 is the only place the figure appears.
AND IT IS CAPPED, WHICH IS THE ONE PLACE THIS LINE PARTS COMPANY WITH ITS NEAR-TWIN ON SCHEDULE SE. Form 4137's own Specific Instruction reads "Line 8. For railroad retirement (RRTA) compensation, don't include an amount greater than $176,100, which is the amount subject to the 6.2% rate for 2025." (lines 127-129). The cap is line 7's own figure, so it is READ FROM /form4137Line7MaxWagesSubjectToOasdi rather than typed a second time — the instruction identifies it as "the amount subject to the 6.2% rate", which is what line 7 is. Schedule SE prints NO such instruction on its line 8a (checked against both https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f1040sse.pdf and https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040sse.pdf: the only 176,100 on that schedule is line 7's own), which is why scheduleSE:/primaryFilerScheduleSeLine8a is uncapped and this fact is not, and why the two cannot be expressed through one another however the rounding is arranged. That fact's FORWARD POINTER — "once that term lands, that module can grow the unrounded sibling and one of these two facts can be expressed through the other" — is falsified by this landing, on substance rather than on shape: an unrounded sibling of this fact would carry a ceiling Schedule SE must not have.
THE CAP BINDS THE PER-FILER TOTAL, NOT EACH W-2. The instruction says not to INCLUDE more than $176,100 of RRTA compensation on the line, and what is included on the line is the total; two railroad W-2s of $100,000 and $90,000 therefore contribute $176,100, not $190,000. THE REJECTED ALTERNATIVE, priced rather than dismissed: a per-employer ceiling, which would let that filer's line 8 read $190,000. It is rejected because the printed sentence governs the amount entered on one line, and because the per-employer reading has no anchor in the instruction's own words; and its stakes are small and stated — whenever either reading's cap can bite, the un-capped RRTA total already exceeds line 7, so line 9 floors to $0 under both and only line 8's own printed entry differs. The boundary case tests/nodes/ty2025/form4137/f4137-line8-rrta-two-w2s-capped-at-the-wage-base holds exactly that pair of W-2s and asserts line 8 = 176,100, which is the only assertion that can tell the two readings apart.
DIRECTION: TAXPAYER-FAVOURABLE, closing a disclosed adverse gap. A larger line 8 leaves a smaller line 9, hence a line 10 at or below its old value, hence line 11 and line 13 at or below theirs. Witnessed by tests/nodes/ty2025/form4137/f4137-line8-rrta-compensation-consumes-base: a railroad filer with $174,000 of box-14 compensation and $3,750 of unreported tips pays $184 of Schedule 2 line-5 tax, against $287 before this term existed.

Fact.Name: Form 4137 line 10 government-employee carve-out, primary filer (the "1.45% tips" dotted-line amount)
Fact.Description:
The amount the line-10 instruction subtracts from line 6 "only for the purpose of comparing lines 6 and 9" — the filer's attestation, BOUNDED ABOVE BY LINE 6.
THE BOUND IS THE WHOLE POINT OF THIS FACT EXISTING SEPARATELY from the writable. The printed instruction subtracts these tips FROM line 6, so they are by construction a subset of line 6; nothing on the form says what to do when a filer attests more. Unclamped, an over-stated attestation would drive the comparison value NEGATIVE, and a negative comparison value flows straight into /primaryFilerForm4137Line10 (whose printed smaller-of carries no floor of its own, unlike lines 4, 6 and 9) and from there into line 11 as a NEGATIVE social security tax — a false allowance manufactured by a data-entry error. The REJECTED alternative is the literal unclamped subtraction; it is rejected because a negative tax line is not a return the law admits and the engine would propagate it silently. Clamped, the same over-statement costs the filer nothing they were owed: line 10 floors at $0 and only the Medicare half of line 13 survives, which is exactly what a filer whose whole line 6 was 1.45%-only employment should pay.

Fact.Name: Form 4137 line 10, primary filer
Fact.Description:

The Specific Instruction lets a filer whose pay was subject only to the 1.45% Medicare tax (federal, state or local government employment) subtract those tips from line 6 "only for the purpose of comparing lines 6 and 9", and then says in terms "Don't reduce the actual entry on line 6." The witness pair is tests/nodes/ty2025/form4137/f4137-government-employee-tips-{carve-out, exceed-line6-clamped}: line 11 moves, line 12 does not.

Fact.Name: A filer's entered Form 4137 line 2 or line 3 is less than that filer's own line 1 rows
Fact.Description:

Fact.Description:
True when THIS filer's own Form 4137 line 6 is positive - the unreported tips left after line 5 removes the months under the $20 threshold, i.e. the tips actually subject to social security and Medicare tax. The per-filer twin of the return-level /form4137RequiredForPrimaryFiler, which stays as the primary filer's own gate and is unchanged.
THE SECONDARY LEG IS GATED ON MFJ, and that is not decoration: a return that was once joint and is no longer can carry a stale secondary tip intake, and without the gate that stale answer would print a whole second Form 4137 for a filer who is not on the return. /secondaryFilerForm4137Line6 is complete-safe $0 on a single-filer return, so the gate is belt and braces and the single-filer case is pinned.
THE TEST IS LINE 6 AND ONLY LINE 6. A wider test - allocated tips in Form W-2 box 8 with a positive line 4 and no line 6 - was proposed with this projection and is NOT built: it changes WHO files the form, which is a substantive ruling and not a print projection, and it is recorded as an open row rather than decided here.

Fact.Name: The filers whose own Form 4137 this return files
Fact.Description:
The collection of filers that file a Form 4137 with this return, one printed copy each. The printed header is the authority - a married couple completes a separate Form 4137 for each spouse with unreported tips - and the register renders one copy per item of this collection, each copy reading that filer's own values through the /filers/*/form4137Printed facts.

The register gated on /form4137RequiredForPrimaryFiler, the PRIMARY filer's line 6 alone, so an MFJ return whose secondary spouse alone had unreported tips rendered no Form 4137 at all even though Schedule 2 line 5 charged her tax. That is the named successor the old gate carried, and this collection closes it.
